summary: Feed s068_single is degraded due to tool overload: 25.49 Gbps microburst exceeds 10 Gbps APM port (255% capacity). All other checks (duplicates, encrypted_share, missing_vlan, one_way, packet_drops) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker forwards bursty aggregate traffic to a single 10 Gbps APM port without load balancing or burst mitigation. A 1 ms microburst peaked at 25.49 Gbps (255% of port capacity, metric 2.549 vs 0.8 threshold) overwhelming port buffers.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will suffer buffer overruns and random packet drops during bursts, leading to incomplete transaction traces, inaccurate latency/error metrics, and missed application performance detections despite needing both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple APM ports with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port utilization below 80% even during 25+ Gbps bursts, preserving bidirectional flow symmetry required by APM and preventing burst-induced drops. Alternatively add slicing since APM needs_full_payload=false, but load balancing directly addresses capacity exceedance.
